analysis.summary: This is a standard-form 10-year franchise agreement (with two 10-year renewal options) under which Airsopure grants a franchisee the right to operate an Airsopure Center using Airsopure's trademarks and system, in an exclusive territory, and to purchase Airsopure's proprietary Products for resale. Airsopure receives (a) a non-refundable $25,000 initial franchise fee (subject to a partial refund contingency if a site is not secured), (b) a continuing 5% royalty on gross sales, (c) a continuing 2% Advertising Fund contribution on gross sales that Airsopure administers at its discretion, (d) a separate 2% local-advertising obligation that the franchisee spends itself (not paid to Airsopure), and (e) revenue from wholesale sales of Products to the franchisee for resale. A personal guarantee (Exhibit F) is contemplated to support collectability, though as a "form" agreement the actual guarantor/signatory and franchisee creditworthiness are not yet known, which is relevant to the Step 1 collectability assessment for any specific executed contract.

obligations.description: Grant of the franchise right/license to use the Airsopure Licensed Marks and system to operate a Center in an exclusive territory, bundled with Airsopure's related pre-opening and ongoing support duties (site approval, initial and continuing training, loan and updates of the Operations Manual, general advisory assistance) that are not distinct from the license because they are highly interrelated with and required to give the franchisee access to the franchise system.
obligations.rationale: The Licensed Marks are symbolic IP - their value derives from Airsopure's ongoing activities (system-wide advertising, brand maintenance, updates) rather than from significant standalone functionality, so this is a right to access IP, recognized over the license period per 606-10-55-58/59/60/62. The pre-opening services (site approval, initial training, manual) and continuing support (advisory assistance, manual updates, ongoing training) are not separately identifiable from the license - a franchisee cannot benefit from training or the manual without the license, and Airsopure integrates these into one franchise-system output (606-10-25-19/25-21/25-22). The combined obligation is satisfied over time as the franchisee simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit of system access throughout the term (606-10-25-27/25-29), recognized over the initial 10-year term.

obligations.description: Continuing royalty of 5% of monthly gross sales, paid as consideration for the franchise license/system.
obligations.rationale: This is a sales-based royalty promised in exchange for a license of IP (the Licensed Marks/franchise system), and the license is the predominant item to which the royalty relates. Under the royalty exception, revenue is recognized as the franchisee's underlying sales occur (i.e., over time, matching the usage that generates the royalty), not estimated up front.

obligations.description: Continuing Advertising Fund contribution of 2% of monthly gross sales, which Airsopure collects, holds in a separate account, and allocates at its sole discretion (with no guarantee of local-market spend) toward system-wide advertising of the Products and Licensed Marks.
obligations.rationale: Airsopure controls the use of these funds (discretion over allocation, right to terminate the fund, no assurance of benefit to any specific franchisee), indicating Airsopure is acting as principal with respect to this fee rather than a mere pass-through/agent for the franchisee. Like the royalty, this fee is usage-based (percentage of gross sales) and paid in exchange for continued access to the franchise system/marks, so it also relates predominantly to the symbolic license; it is recognized as the underlying sales occur, consistent with the royalty exception approach.

obligations.description: Wholesale sale of Airsopure's proprietary Products to the franchisee (opening order and subsequent reorders) for resale to end customers in the exclusive territory.
obligations.rationale: Airsopure sets prices, controls availability/allocation, and ships the goods; the franchisee obtains control (physical possession, risk of loss on freight-collect shipment, right to resell at its own set prices) at shipment/delivery. This is a distinct promise separable from the license - the franchisee can benefit from the goods together with its own resale efforts, and product sales are priced and transacted separately from the license/royalty fees. Each order is satisfied at the point in time control transfers to the franchisee.

consideration.summary: Transaction price to Airsopure comprises: (1) a fixed $25,000 initial franchise fee, contingently refundable up to 70% if a Center site is not agreed within 4 months (a variable element/constraint on the otherwise-fixed fee prior to site selection); (2) variable, usage-based fees tied to the franchisee's gross sales - a 5% royalty and a 2% Advertising Fund contribution, both paid to Airsopure in exchange for the franchise license; and (3) variable amounts for wholesale Product purchases, priced at Airsopure's then-prevailing prices and quantities ordered. analysis.summary: eGain provides Eliance with hosted (SaaS) access to eGain's software for processing online customer inquiries, plus 24/7 live telephone support, under a one-year renewable hosting agreement. The Customer never takes possession of the software; the small client-side download exists solely to enable use of the hosted service and carries no independent value, so no separate software license performance obligation arises (ASC 985-20-15-5, 606-10-55-54). The contract is enforceable, with defined payment terms, cure rights and no indication of collectability doubt, so it qualifies as a contract under ASC 606-10-25-1/-2. The core promise is a stand-ready hosting/access obligation recognized over time, together with over-time customer support. Consideration is a fixed periodic hosting fee (subject to renewal-date price adjustment) plus possible "Additional Fees" for usage not quantified in the visible contract, and SLA-driven service credits for Downtime that function as a price concession (variable consideration, constrained to the amount to which eGain has an enforceable right at each period). No sales- or usage-based IP royalty applies because this is a hosted-service fee arrangement, not a right-to-use license of IP.

obligations.description: Web-based hosted access to eGain's software (the 'Hosting Services') running on eGain's servers/eGain System, enabling Customer to process and respond to online inquiries ('Online Messages') from its Users, together with access to usage Reports via a password-protected site. Any de minimis client-side software components downloaded to Customer's/User's computer are licensed solely for use in connection with the Hosting Services and have no standalone functionality outside the hosted service, so they do not constitute a separate license performance obligation.
obligations.rationale: Customer cannot take possession of eGain's core software and run it on its own or a third party's hardware; it only accesses eGain-hosted functionality, which is a hosted service rather than a license under ASC 985-20-15-5/606-10-55-54. The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit of access as eGain provides it (606-10-25-27), and successive monthly/daily increments of access are substantially the same and measured the same way, so they form a series recognized over time (606-10-25-14/-15). Termination provisions confirm access ceases immediately upon termination and unpaid fees are due only through that date, consistent with a stand-ready access obligation rather than delivery of a good.

JHU is a research university with no ability or obligation to further develop, support, or maintain the technology (c-038); prosecution/maintenance of the underlying patents is performed by JHU at its sole discretion for its own benefit, not as a service promised to the customer (c-025). Consequently the contract contains a single performance obligation: the grant of a functional IP license, satisfied at a point in time when the license is granted/rights become exercisable. Consideration is a mix of a fixed license fee (cash + equity), an annual minimum royalty that is creditable against earned running royalties (in substance a guaranteed minimum), an uncapped sales/usage-based running royalty on Net Sales/Net Service Revenues, and a contingent "Liquidity Event"/IPO fee tied to a change-of-control or public-offering valuation event. The running royalty qualifies for the sales- or usage-based royalty exception because the license is the sole/predominant item to which it relates; the Liquidity Event fee does not qualify for that exception (it is not tied to sales/usage of licensed products/services but to a corporate transaction) and is therefore evaluated—and largely constrained—under the general variable consideration guidance.

obligations.description: Non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide license under JHU's Patent Right(s) (Exhibit C - Active Cannulas technology) to make, have made, import, offer for sale and sell Licensed Products, and to perform Licensed Services, in the Licensed Field (Cannulated Surgical Intervention). No sublicensing permitted. JHU provides no ongoing development, updates, or support; the patent as it exists is licensed 'as is' (c-039), and JHU's continued patent prosecution (c-025) is for JHU's own benefit/discretion, not a promised customer service. Title to the underlying technology remains with JHU and all rights revert to JHU on termination/expiration (c-030), consistent with a right to use existing IP rather than a right to access evolving IP.
obligations.rationale: This is functional IP (an existing patented invention with standalone functionality, not a brand/franchise whose value depends on JHU's ongoing activities). Per ASC 606-10-55-58 through 55-62, a license to functional IP is a right to use the IP as it exists at the point the license is granted, and is recognized at a point in time - here, when the license becomes effective and Virtuoso obtains the right to use, make and sell under the patents (control transfers at grant since JHU has no further performance obligations tied to the license itself; c-013, c-025, c-039). There is no service, hosting, or symbolic/brand element that would call for over-time recognition.

JHU is a research university with no ability or obligation to further develop, support, or maintain the technology (c-038); prosecution/maintenance of the underlying patents is performed by JHU at its sole discretion for its own benefit, not as a service promised to the customer (c-025). Consequently the contract contains a single performance obligation: the grant of a functional IP license, satisfied at a point in time when the license is granted/rights become exercisable. Consideration is a mix of a fixed license fee (cash + equity), an annual minimum royalty that is creditable against earned running royalties (in substance a guaranteed minimum), an uncapped sales/usage-based running royalty on Net Sales/Net Service Revenues, and a contingent "Liquidity Event"/IPO fee tied to a change-of-control or public-offering valuation event. The running royalty qualifies for the sales- or usage-based royalty exception because the license is the sole/predominant item to which it relates; the Liquidity Event fee does not qualify for that exception (it is not tied to sales/usage of licensed products/services but to a corporate transaction) and is therefore evaluated—and largely constrained—under the general variable consideration guidance.

obligations.description: Non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide license under JHU's Patent Right(s) (Exhibit C - Active Cannulas technology) to make, have made, import, offer for sale and sell Licensed Products, and to perform Licensed Services, in the Licensed Field (Cannulated Surgical Intervention). No sublicensing permitted. JHU provides no ongoing development, updates, or support; the patent as it exists is licensed 'as is' (c-039), and JHU's continued patent prosecution (c-025) is for JHU's own benefit/discretion, not a promised customer service. Title to the underlying technology remains with JHU and all rights revert to JHU on termination/expiration (c-030), consistent with a right to use existing IP rather than a right to access evolving IP.
obligations.rationale: This is functional IP (an existing patented invention with standalone functionality, not a brand/franchise whose value depends on JHU's ongoing activities). Per ASC 606-10-55-58 through 55-62, a license to functional IP is a right to use the IP as it exists at the point the license is granted, and is recognized at a point in time - here, when the license becomes effective and Virtuoso obtains the right to use, make and sell under the patents (control transfers at grant since JHU has no further performance obligations tied to the license itself; c-013, c-025, c-039). There is no service, hosting, or symbolic/brand element that would call for over-time recognition.

consideration.summary: Consideration consists of: (1) a fixed, nonrefundable $2,000 cash license fee plus a grant of common stock equal to 5% of Virtuoso's fully-diluted capitalization, due within 30 days of the effective date and not creditable against royalties (c-015, c-049, c-050); (2) a $3,000 minimum annual royalty due on each anniversary, fully creditable (non-cumulatively) against running/earned royalties paid during the preceding year (c-016, c-054, c-055); (3) an uncapped running/earned royalty of 4% of Net Sales and Net Service Revenues from Licensed Products/Services, subject to royalty-stacking credits and Least-Developed-Country carve-outs (c-017, c-051, c-052, c-053); and (4) a contingent 'Liquidity Event' fee of 1% of Aggregate Consideration (on a merger, stock sale or asset sale) or, for an IPO, 1% of Pre-Money Valuation, payable only on the first such triggering event, including any later 'Trailing Consideration' (c-056, c-057, c-058, c-059, c-060, c-061).
consideration.rationale: The $2,000 cash fee and the equity grant are fixed consideration for the license (measured at fair value of the equity at contract inception under noncash-consideration principles) and are recognized when the license transfers (point in time). The running royalty (4% of Net Sales/Net Service Revenues) is a sales- or usage-based royalty promised in exchange for a license of IP where the license is the sole performance obligation/predominant item to which the royalty relates, so under the royalty exception (606-10-55-65 through 55-65B) it is not estimated at contract inception; it is recognized only as the underlying sales/services occur (later of usage and satisfaction of the license PO, which here has already occurred). The $3,000 minimum annual royalty is fully creditable against earned royalty for that year only, so in substance it functions as a guaranteed minimum/floor on the sales-based royalty rather than a truly fixed fee; judgment is required (see open questions) as to whether the minimum should be treated as fixed consideration recognized at license grant, with only royalties in excess of the minimum following the royalty exception, consistent with common minimum-guarantee fact patterns. The Liquidity Event/IPO fee is variable consideration tied to a future corporate transaction (change of control or public offering), not to sales or usage of the Licensed Products/Services, so the IP royalty exception does not apply; instead it is evaluated under the general constraint (606-10-32-5 through 32-8) and, given the high uncertainty of whether/when a liquidity event or IPO will occur and its magnitude (dependent on future enterprise valuation), is fully constrained (excluded from the transaction price) until the triggering event occurs and the amount can be reliably estimated.

analysis.summary: Developer agreed to design, build and deliver a custom mobile/web application ("Pelican Delivers Application Phase 1") for Pelican Delivers Inc. under a fixed, milestone-billed Statement of Work (Appendix A). The Agreement is a validly formed, enforceable contract (c-001, c-002, c-003) with identifiable rights and payment terms (c-050) and no indicators of collectability problems (a 20% deposit is collected upfront and milestone payments are due as work is accepted). The core promise is a single, highly-integrated custom software build (POS integration, Maps API, payment processing, ID verification, reporting, driver-app improvements, and a customer-facing portal) that is not separately identifiable from Developer's other Phase 1 tasks, so it is accounted for as one combined services performance obligation, recognized over time. IP in the finished Deliverables is assigned to the Client as work-for-hire (c-019); Developer does not grant Pelican a license to use Developer's own IP that would create a separate license performance obligation - Developer's retained pre-existing technology (c-020) is incidental background IP used to perform the service, not a distinct promised good or service. A discretionary early-completion Bonus (c-017) and elective post-termination hourly transition assistance (c-013, c-034) are additional variable/optional items that are analyzed separately below.

obligations.description: Custom design, development, and delivery of the integrated Pelican Delivers Phase 1 application (POS integration, Google Maps API, payment processing, ID verification, reporting, driver-app workflow, and customer portal website), delivered and tested across four contractual Milestones plus a Final Deliverable, with ownership of the resulting Works assigned to Client as work-made-for-hire.
obligations.rationale: The SOW components are highly interdependent parts of one custom application rather than separately identifiable outputs (ASC 606-10-25-19/21/22), so they are combined into a single performance obligation. Recognition is over time because (i) the work-for-hire structure means Client obtains control of the Works as they are created (606-10-25-27(b)), and (ii) the custom, client-specific design has no alternative use to Developer while Developer has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date - milestone deposits, milestone-linked fee tranches, and the termination provisions requiring Client to pay for all Services/Deliverables performed through the termination date (606-10-25-27(c)).

obligations.description: Optional post-termination/expiration Termination Assistance Services (knowledge transfer, documentation return, data-migration assistance) billed at an additional hourly rate of $125/hour if elected by Client.
obligations.rationale: This is a distinct service that the customer can benefit from separately and that is priced at what appears to be a standalone hourly rate; it is only provided if elected, so it is not a present performance obligation of the base contract but a service Developer stands ready to perform on election. If elected, it would be recognized over time as hours are worked, consistent with a service satisfied through the customer simultaneously receiving and consuming the benefit (606-10-25-27(a)).

consideration.summary: Transaction price is predominantly fixed: $279,000 for Phase 1, payable as a 20% deposit plus four 20% milestone tranches tied to Milestone acceptance (c-050). Two additional items introduce variability: (1) a discretionary early-completion Bonus (amount referenced but not quantified in the excerpts reviewed) payable only if Developer finishes ahead of the Final Delivery Date and Client accepts the Deliverables (c-017); and (2) optional hourly Termination Assistance Services billed at $125/hour if elected (c-013, c-034), which are consideration for a separate, optional service rather than part of the fixed Phase-1 price. No sales- or usage-based IP royalty exists in this contract because Developer does not license its own IP to Client for the Client's downstream commercial exploitation on a usage basis - instead Developer assigns ownership of the custom Works to Client for fixed/milestone fees; Developer's retained "Developer Technology" (c-020) is not licensed to Client at all (Client explicitly may not use it independently), so the royalty exception in 606-10-55-65 is not applicable.
consideration.rationale: The Bonus is a performance-based incentive tied to early, accepted completion, and the Termination Assistance fee is usage/hours-based - both are variable consideration under 606-10-32-5/32-6, requiring estimation (likely most-likely-amount method for the Bonus, given the binary accept/reject-by-date nature) and application of the constraint in 606-10-32-11/32-12 - the Bonus should only be included in the transaction price to the extent it is probable there will not be a significant revenue reversal, which depends on Developer's progress relative to the schedule and its historical experience meeting delivery dates, both of which are uncertain from the contract text alone. No royalty exception applies because there is no license of Developer's IP to the Client with usage-based royalties; the Client is instead the owner/assignee of the custom Works.

open_questions: The dollar amount or formula for the early-completion Bonus is referenced in Section 5.3 (c-017) as 'detailed in the applicable SOW,' but no such amount appears in the SOW excerpts reviewed (c-046-c-058); its magnitude and probability of achievement need confirmation from Developer's project records to estimate variable consideration and apply the constraint.

Whether the SOW component features (POS integration, Maps API, payment processing, ID verification, driver app, customer portal) could be viewed by Developer as separately distinct performance obligations with standalone selling prices, versus one integrated build, is a judgment call - here treated as one combined obligation due to high interdependency, but if Developer regularly sells any of these modules independently, a multiple-element allocation may be more appropriate.

Change Orders (Section 4) may add distinct, separately priced scope; each executed Change Order/amended SOW should be evaluated at execution to determine whether it is a separate contract or a modification requiring prospective or cumulative catch-up treatment (606-10-25-10/12/13); none were included in the base facts reviewed.

No explicit representation regarding Client's creditworthiness or history of payment is in the contract; collectability is assumed probable based on the deposit and milestone structure, but this should be corroborated with Developer's credit assessment of Pelican Delivers Inc.

Whether Developer's Bonus and Termination Assistance fees are priced at observable standalone selling prices (needed for allocation, though here they attach to non-distinct/optional items rather than requiring formal allocation) should be confirmed.

obligations.rationale: The SOW components are highly interdependent parts of one custom application rather than separately identifiable outputs (ASC 606-10-25-19/21/22), so they are combined into a single performance obligation. Recognition is over time because (i) the work-for-hire structure means Client obtains control of the Works as they are created (606-10-25-27(b)), and (ii) the custom, client-specific design has no alternative use to Developer while Developer has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date - milestone deposits, milestone-linked fee tranches, and the termination provisions requiring Client to pay for all Services/Deliverables performed through the termination date (606-10-25-27(c)).

obligations.description: Optional post-termination/expiration Termination Assistance Services (knowledge transfer, documentation return, data-migration assistance) billed at an additional hourly rate of $125/hour if elected by Client.
obligations.rationale: This is a distinct service that the customer can benefit from separately and that is priced at what appears to be a standalone hourly rate; it is only provided if elected, so it is not a present performance obligation of the base contract but a service Developer stands ready to perform on election. If elected, it would be recognized over time as hours are worked, consistent with a service satisfied through the customer simultaneously receiving and consuming the benefit (606-10-25-27(a)).

consideration.summary: Transaction price is predominantly fixed: $279,000 for Phase 1, payable as a 20% deposit plus four 20% milestone tranches tied to Milestone acceptance (c-050). Two additional items introduce variability: (1) a discretionary early-completion Bonus (amount referenced but not quantified in the excerpts reviewed) payable only if Developer finishes ahead of the Final Delivery Date and Client accepts the Deliverables (c-017); and (2) optional hourly Termination Assistance Services billed at $125/hour if elected (c-013, c-034), which are consideration for a separate, optional service rather than part of the fixed Phase-1 price. No sales- or usage-based IP royalty exists in this contract because Developer does not license its own IP to Client for the Client's downstream commercial exploitation on a usage basis - instead Developer assigns ownership of the custom Works to Client for fixed/milestone fees; Developer's retained "Developer Technology" (c-020) is not licensed to Client at all (Client explicitly may not use it independently), so the royalty exception in 606-10-55-65 is not applicable.
consideration.rationale: The Bonus is a performance-based incentive tied to early, accepted completion, and the Termination Assistance fee is usage/hours-based - both are variable consideration under 606-10-32-5/32-6, requiring estimation (likely most-likely-amount method for the Bonus, given the binary accept/reject-by-date nature) and application of the constraint in 606-10-32-11/32-12 - the Bonus should only be included in the transaction price to the extent it is probable there will not be a significant revenue reversal, which depends on Developer's progress relative to the schedule and its historical experience meeting delivery dates, both of which are uncertain from the contract text alone. No royalty exception applies because there is no license of Developer's IP to the Client with usage-based royalties; the Client is instead the owner/assignee of the custom Works.

Change Orders (Section 4) may add distinct, separately priced scope; each executed Change Order/amended SOW should be evaluated at execution to determine whether it is a separate contract or a modification requiring prospective or cumulative catch-up treatment (606-10-25-10/12/13); none were included in the base facts reviewed.

No explicit representation regarding Client's creditworthiness or history of payment is in the contract; collectability is assumed probable based on the deposit and milestone structure, but this should be corroborated with Developer's credit assessment of Pelican Delivers Inc.

Whether Developer's Bonus and Termination Assistance fees are priced at observable standalone selling prices (needed for allocation, though here they attach to non-distinct/optional items rather than requiring formal allocation) should be confirmed.
